supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 recorded a network logon for raj.patel from WS-RPATEL-01; at 13:44 UTC, PowerShell ran under raj.patel using the same logon ID.

The PowerShell command ran the inventory-listed IT patch script, \\FILE-PIN-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1. Its child process launched wusa to install a Windows update, consistent with the stated patching practice and calendar.
The PowerShell process made a proxy connection transferring about 38.8 MB, created a temporary file, and then exited; wusa also exited shortly afterward.

known_telemetry_limitations: The logs establish a PowerShell process at 13:44 UTC, but do not establish that this was the window Ana Ruiz saw or whether it was visible on screen.
The script contents, downloaded payload provenance, and integrity of the installed update are not provided.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the exact time or visual appearance of the reported window.
The evidence does not independently verify that the patch script or update payload was unmodified.
unrelated_findings: At 13:23 UTC, Ana Ruiz ran a separate hidden PowerShell command to export up to 200 Security log events to C:\Reports\audit.csv. This precedes the reported approximate time and is not the later IT patch process; assess separately. Records: T094-00030, T094-00031.

Around 13:23 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 resolved WS-TWEBER-01 and established a TLS connection to it; the available records do not identify the connection's purpose. Assess separately. Records: T094-00033, T094-00037, T094-00038, T094-00040.

A 13:23 UTC NTLM validation and network logon on WS-ESTONE-01 identify tom.weber with WS-ARUIZ-01 as the workstation. Later, records show authentication involving raj.patel and tom.weber from WS-ARUIZ-01 to their respective workstations. These are outside the identified patch process and merit separate review; they do not determine this alert. Records: T094-00015, T094-00016, T094-00230, T094-00231, T094-00233, T094-00237, T094-00238, T094-00241.
